events.title: Spring Boot 2.0 released
events.summary: Pivotal released Spring Boot 2.0 on March 1, 2018 — adding reactive WebFlux, Java 8 baseline, and Spring Framework 5 support.
events.about: Spring Boot 2.0 brought non-blocking Netty servers, Micrometer metrics, and HTTP/2 defaults — the stack teams used for microservices through the late 2010s. It aligned with Spring 5's reactive programming story while keeping the `java -jar` simplicity that made Boot popular.

narrative.whyChosen: Spring Boot 2.0 made reactive Java microservices production-viable.
narrative.whyImportant: WebFlux and Micrometer integrated observability and async I/O into the default Boot stack.
narrative.problemSolved: Blocking servlet stacks struggled with high-concurrency APIs and cloud-native metrics.

sources.title: Spring Blog — Spring Boot 2.0 Goes GA (March 1, 2018)

events.title: Samsung Galaxy S9 released
events.summary: Samsung began selling the Samsung Galaxy S9 — variable aperture camera and AR Emoji — iterative S-line update.
events.about: The Galaxy S series remained Android's volume flagship counterweight to iPhone. Variable aperture camera and ar emoji — iterative s-line update. Developers testing Android builds routinely validated on Galaxy S hardware as the default non-Pixel reference.

narrative.whyChosen: The Samsung Galaxy S9 continued Samsung's annual Android flagship cadence.
narrative.whyImportant: Galaxy S devices set the hardware bar millions of Android users and developers encounter.
narrative.problemSolved: Android needed consistent premium hardware for testing flagship features each year.
